summary: Create retention-policy matrix and automation for cross-pod onboarding channels
description: Issue summary: We need a canonical retention-policy matrix and an accompanying Slack/Confluence automation to enforce onboarding channel lifecycle behavior for cross-pod channels. Rationale: teams repeatedly request ad-hoc channel creation for short-lived experiments and onboarding. Without a standard retention matrix and automation, channels remain active indefinitely creating noise, compliance risk, and searchability issues.
background: Currently there is a loose set of archival practices documented across multiple Confluence pages; enforcement is manual. Recent audit flagged 23 onboarding channels older than 180 days with active bots and no owners. Pod leads frequently ask for retention exceptions but there's no consistent approval or snapshot workflow.
request_details: 1) Create a retention-policy matrix that maps channel types (pod-standup, onboarding, ephemeral-experiment, partner-bridge, review) to default retention windows, snapshot cadences, owner handoff rules, and archive actions. 2) Implement Slack automation (bot) to: - apply a retention tag on channel creation based on naming suffix/pod tag, - send owner nudges 30/15/3 days before archive, - create a Confluence snapshot page in a designated space when channel reaches 90 days and again at archive, - require an approval workflow for exceptions via a Jira ticket template. 3) Add a guardrail in the onboarding flow so ephemeral channels created via the pod-bootstrap tool default to the ephemeral-experiment policy.
impact: Operational: reduces channel sprawl and search noise. Compliance: ensures audit snapshots and owner attestations are captured. Productivity: fewer stale channels for new hires to sift through. Expected to reduce support noise related to channel archival requests by ~40%.
steps: 1) Draft the retention-policy matrix and get sign-off from Pod Ops, Security, and Legal. 2) Prototype Slack bot flow in staging using @retention-bot user with approvals routed to jira-project 'INT'. 3) Implement Confluence snapshot template and automation to attach snapshots to generated Jira exceptions. 4) Rollout to two pilot pods (Model Eval and Runtime Ops) for 4 weeks, collect feedback, then global rollout.
technical_implementation_notes: - Slack bot will use SCIM identifiers and channel metadata to infer pod tag. - Use Slack scheduled messages for 30/15/3-day nudges. - Confluence snapshots created via REST API v2; pages stored under 'Pod-Onboarding Snapshots' with explicit ACLs. - Approval flow created as a Jira Service Desk template with 'retention-exception' label. - Automation scripts will be authored in the existing automation repo (git@github.com:redwood/ops-automation.git) and deployed via the platform's pipeline.

investigation_notes: Initial audit shows 23 channels >180 days labelled 'onboarding' but three of those are active partner-bridges that require exception handling. Identified missing channel metadata on creation for roughly 18% of channels (no 'pod:' tag), which will require patching the pod-bootstrap lambda to include tags.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification of channels leading to premature archival. Mitigation: conservative default windows, owner nudges and blocking archive until owner response or escalation to retention-admins. Rollback: a one-click 'reopen-last-archive' tool for 7 days after archive.
resolution: (pending) Prototype bot implemented in staging and retention matrix draft v0.1 reviewed by Security. Full rollout blocked on Legal sign-off for partner-bridge policy and on a small fix to pod-bootstrap tag propagation.
